newsitem.title: USA: Mississippi River at Baton Rouge closed.
newsitem.headline: Mississippi River at Baton Rouge closed.

text.p: The Mississippi River remains closed indefinitely as workers scramble to clean up after a tow of 25 barges hit a bridge in north Baton Rouge late Monday, the Coast Guard said Tuesday.

No injuries were reported, but two rock barges sank, two were beached and one is missing, while a tank barge carrying a mix of benzene and gasoline capsized and is aground on the west bank of the river, the Coast Guard said.
An unknown quantity of the petro-chemical product has leaked, and local officials ordered a precautionary evacuation of residents and businesses in the vicinity, authorities said.
Ingram Barge Co, owner of the capsized barge, has contracted with Oil Mop Inc for cleanup, Woodward Clyde for air monitoring and McKinney Salvage, the Coast Guard said.

Only tows with no more than two barges are being permitted to move in the accident area, a Coast Guard spokesman said. "Judging from the number of phone calls we've gotten, there must be a lot of traffic backing up there just like on the freeway," he said.
Flooding north of Louisiana and heavy rains have created high water and swift current conditions on the river. The cause of the accident is under investigation.
